oneLiner.en: At Kever Rochel on the last day of Av, the Mashgiach explains Elul as the month Yaakov 'grabbed' back from Esav, traces the power of grabbing to Rochel's self-giving and to Binyamin, and calls for grabbing oneself out of today's trials through Torah together with tefillah.

abstract.en: Speaking at Kever Rochel as Av ends, the Mashgiach brings the Zohar that Yaakov 'grabbed' the month of Elul from Esav, and a Midrash about a maiden who grabbed an angel's wings and was set as Elul's mazal, Besulah. Since a mazal is the flow of influence on its month, Elul's influence is grabbing: a person should grab from the sitra achra, not be grabbed by it. He then turns to Rochel, whose soul left with Binyamin's birth, and to the Midrash where Hashem forgives Israel in the merit of her giving her signs to her sister. Binyamin, her quintessence, has the power to grab back, as on Tu B'Av when his tribe grabbed wives at Shiloh. Sitting at Rochel's grave, the Mashgiach calls for a resolution not to be grabbed by the yetzer hara, laments young men caught by electronic devices, and insists that Torah and tefillah must go together, recommending Rebbe Elimelech's tefillah before Shabbos davening.

en: Following the Zohar, the Mashgiach explains that Elul is a month Yaakov grabbed for himself from Esav's portion.
A mazal is the source of influence that flows onto its month, so the influence of Elul is the power to grab: to take from the sitra achra rather than be taken by it.
Rochel's soul left together with Binyamin's birth, so Binyamin is the quintessence of his mother.
Tu B'Av became a day of grabbing through Binyamin, whose tribe grabbed wives at Shiloh, and from then on Yaakov's portion can be grabbed back.
The Mashgiach says Torah and tefillah must go together, and that this is the only counsel for the trials of our time.

title.en: Kever Rochel and the grabbed month of Elul

summary.en: The Mashgiach opens at Kever Rochel, saying the whole area is Rochel's place, and speaks of Rochel as mother of the Jewish people. He brings the Zohar that the months were divided between Yaakov and Esav and that Yaakov went and grabbed Elul.

title.en: The mazal of Elul and the power to grab

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings a Midrash that a maiden grabbed the wings of one of the fallen angels, flew up to the Kisei HaKavod and was set as the mazal Besulah, the mazal of Elul. He explains that a mazal is the flow of influence on its month, so Elul's influence is grabbing: a person must grab from the sitra achra and not let himself be grabbed by the desires of the times.

title.en: Rochel's passing, Binyamin and her plea

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Rochel's soul left as Binyamin was born, and since the moment of passing holds the essence of a whole life, Binyamin is her quintessence. He brings the Midrash in which the Avos and Moshe pleaded in vain and Hashem forgave Israel for Rochel, who gave her signs to her sister, and the passuk promising that her children will return. Because Binyamin carries her self-giving, he has the merit to grab back what Esav wants for himself, since all of creation belongs to Yisrael.

title.en: Binyamin grabs: Tu B'Av and Kislev

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells of the war with Binyamin, the oath not to give them wives, and the advice to grab the daughters dancing at Shiloh, as in Sefer Shoftim; this was on Tu B'Av, which the Gemara counts as a yom tov for this reason. He explains that from Tu B'Av on the portion is Yaakov's, that the day became a day of grabbing through Binyamin, and that Binyamin's month Kislev also grabs days of Teves for Chanukah.

title.en: A resolution at Rochel's grave as Av ends

summary.en: On the last day of Av, sitting at the grave of Rochel, the root of grabbing, the Mashgiach calls for a resolution not to let the yetzer hara grab, which he calls the avodah of Elul that Yaakov began. He laments the fine young men who come to him caught by today's electronic devices, says breaking out takes real self-sacrifice, and that everyone is affected to some degree.

title.en: Torah together with tefillah

summary.en: The Mashgiach says that one cannot have tefillah without Torah nor Torah without tefillah, and tells of a young man who came crying to the Satmar Rav that he could not rid himself of bad thoughts. He stresses that no one can be sure when a sudden trial will come, that Torah with tefillah is the only counsel, and calls on all to enter the grabbed month of Elul grabbing with Torah and good middos, not foolishness.

title.en: Good davening and Rebbe Elimelech's tefillah

summary.en: The Mashgiach calls good davening the best counsel and recalls great men who came to tefillah with deep seriousness, naming Rabbi Shlomo Heiman, Rabbi Yisrael Chaim Kaplan and Rabbi Reuven Grozovsky. He speaks of chevlei Moshiach, says Rebbe Elimelech nullified them through tefillah, and recommends saying Rebbe Elimelech's tefillah on Shabbos morning before davening, taking ten minutes to plead before Hashem.
